extracted.intended_audience: users of PARI/GP (computational number theorists and mathematicians) who compute elliptic-curve invariants and perform arithmetic with elliptic curves
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP elliptic-curve functions: input formats, preconditions, return values, normalization conventions, and usage notes for computing invariants, points, isogenies, p-adic quantities, and other arithmetic on elliptic curves.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellgroup: group structure of non-singular points (flag behavior)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute structure of the (cyclic) group of non-singular points for the reduction of a minimal model at p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag = 0, the equation need not be minimal or even integral at p; minimal model is more efficient. If flag = 1, requested generators depend on the model, which must be minimal at p or an exception is thrown; use ellintegralmodel and/or elllocalred first. Also warns about inconsistent moduli when working with mixed domains (examples show usage over Q, Mod(1,11) and finite fields). Library syntax: GEN ellgroup0(GEN E, GEN p = NULL, long flag). GEN ellgroup(GEN E, GEN p) corresponds to flag = 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellheegner: Heegner-point method preconditions and complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Given E/Q assumed of (analytic) rank 1, returns a non-torsion rational point whose canonical height equals the product of the elliptic regulator by the analytic Sha.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses Heegner point method (Cohen GTM 239). Complexity proportional to sqrt(conductor) * height, so preferable on strong Weil curves. If curve has rank 0 or even analytic rank, an error is raised. Syntax: GEN ellheegner(GEN E).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellheight: Néron–Tate height computation and normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute global Néron–Tate height h(P) of point P on elliptic curve E over Q or a number field, using Cremona's normalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E must be an ell as output by ellinit; minimal model not required but makes computation faster. If Q is provided, computes bilinear form (h(P+Q)-h(P-Q))/4. Syntax: GEN ellheight0(GEN E, GEN P, GEN Q = NULL, long prec) and GEN ellheight(GEN E, GEN P, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellheightmatrix: height Gram matrix and regulator relation
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a vector x of points, returns the Gram matrix of Néron–Tate heights; rank approximates rank of set, determinant equals regulator if x is a Mordell–Weil basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Height normalization follows Cremona; matrix should be divided by 2 to match Silverman's normalization. Syntax: GEN ellheightmatrix(GEN E, GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellidentify: look up curve in elldata
rubrics_metrics.description: Look up elliptic curve E (arbitrary model over Q) in elldata database; return [[N, M, G], C] with Cremona name N, minimal model M, Z-basis G of free part, and change-of-coordinates C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: GEN ellidentify(GEN E). Useful to retrieve canonical labels and generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellinit: acceptable input forms and domain D handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Initialize an ell structure attached to an elliptic curve. E may be 5-component [a1,a2,a3,a4,a6], 2-component [a4,a6] (short Weierstrass), or a Cremona string like '11a1'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional D argument describes domain (default t_INT 1 = Q), can be prime p for F_p, Mod(a,p) for F_p, t_FFELT for F_q, t_PADIC for Q_p with given precision, t_REAL for complex numbers (precision from realprecision), number field (nf or bnf) or a prime ideal (prid). D is indicative: coefficients checked for compatibility and inconsistencies raise errors (example: inconsistent moduli). If coefficients are too general, only basic operations supported. Singular curves return [] and fail. Resulting ell structure contains at least a1,a2,a3,a4,a6,b2,b4,b6,b8,c4,c6,Delta,j accessible via members. Some domain-specific data are computed lazily and cached. Syntax: GEN ellinit(GEN x, GEN D = NULL, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellintegralmodel: obtain integral model and change of variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Return an integral model for an ell structure E over a number field K or Qp; optionally set v to [u,0,0,0] giving the change of variables (same form as ellchangecurve).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows returned integral coefficients and v. Syntax: GEN ellintegralmodel(GEN E, GEN *v = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellisdivisible: test n-divisibility and complexity advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Given E/K a number field and P in E(K), return 1 if P = [n]R for some R in E(K) and set Q to one such R; return 0 otherwise. Integer n ≥ 0; can be ellxn(E,n) if many tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algebraic complexity is O(n^4), so advisable to factor n and use chained checks on prime divisors; function will factor n itself unless n is in ellxn form. Syntax: long ellisdivisible(GEN E, GEN P, GEN n, GEN *Q = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellisogeny: compute quotient curve and isogeny rational functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Given elliptic curve E and finite subgroup G (either a generator for cyclic G or a polynomial vanishing on x-coordinates of non-zero elements), return [a1,a2,a3,a4,a6] invariants of E/G and, unless only_image=1, a vector [f,g,h] of rational functions giving the isogeny (x,y) -> (f(x)/h(x)^2, g(x,y)/h(x)^3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: only_image flag = 1 returns only the image curve (saves time). x,y optional variable numbers. Syntax: GEN ellisogeny(GEN E, GEN G, long only_image, long x = -1, long y = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellisogenyapply: apply isogeny to point or compose isogenies
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply an isogeny f (result of ellisogeny) to g: if g is a point, return f(g); if g is a compatible isogeny, return composition f ◦ g.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show applying to points and composing isogenies. Syntax: GEN ellisogenyapply(GEN f, GEN g).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellisomat: compute isogenous curves and degree matrix
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute representatives of isomorphism classes of elliptic curves Q-isogenous to E. Returns [L,M] where L lists triples [Ei, fi, gi] (Ei in [a4,a6] form, fi:E->Ei, gi dual) and M is matrix of isogeny degrees between Ei and Ej. First curve E1 is isomorphic to E by f1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag fl=1 skips computing fi,gi and returns only curves Ei (faster). p parameter restricts to isogenies of degree a power of p. Over number fields possible degrees determined by Billerey algorithm; CM curves over number fields not fully supported. Syntax: GEN ellisomat(GEN E, long p, long fl).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellisoncurve: point-on-curve test tolerant to imprecise coefficients
rubrics_metrics.description: Return 1 if point z is on elliptic curve E, 0 otherwise. If E or z have imprecise coefficients, an approximate equality check is attempted. If z is a vector of points, returns a vector of same type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also available: int oncurve(GEN E, GEN z) which does not accept vectors of points. Syntax: GEN ellisoncurve(GEN E, GEN z).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellisotree: isogeny tree (adjacency matrix) and minimal models
rubrics_metrics.description: Given E or a set of Q-isogenous curves, return [L,M] where L lists minimal models of isomorphism classes and M is adjacency matrix of prime-degree isogeny tree: edge from Ei to Ej if there is a prime-degree isogeny preserving Néron differential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples compare results to ellisomat and allow restriction by prime degrees via ellisomat arguments. Syntax: GEN ellisotree(GEN E).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellissupersingular: supersingularity test and input requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Return 1 if elliptic curve E (over number field, Qp or finite field) is supersingular at p, 0 otherwise. If curve defined over a number field, p must be explicitly given (prime number or maximal ideal). Returns 1 iff E has supersingular good reduction at p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively, E can be given by its j-invariant in a finite field (omit p). Also available: int elljissupersingular(GEN j) for j-invariant input. Syntax: GEN ellissupersingular(GEN E, GEN p = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellj: elliptic j-invariant computation domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute elliptic j-invariant; input x must be a complex number with positive imaginary part, or convertible into a power series or a p-adic number with positive valuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN jell(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: elllocalred: Kodaira type, conductor exponent, change-of-coordinates and Tamagawa
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute Kodaira type of local fiber of E at p. Returns 4-component vector [f, kod, v, c] where f is exponent of p in arithmetic conductor, kod codes Kodaira type, v = [u,r,s,t] gives coordinate changes done during local reduction (u=1 iff equation was already minimal at p), and c is local Tamagawa number cp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kodaira coding: 1 = good reduction (I0), 2,3,4 = II, III, IV etc; 4+ν with ν>0 means Iν; negative values represent starred types I* etc. E must be an ell from ellinit; p omitted implies p=(?) over Q—(note: text suggests p better left omitted when over Q). Syntax: GEN elllocalred(GEN E, GEN p = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: elllog: discrete logarithm on E/Fq with order parameter option
rubrics_metrics.description: Return discrete logarithm n such that P = [n]G on elliptic curve E/Fq. If present, o represents order of G (preferred format [N,factor(N)]). If o omitted, assume G generates curve. Function also assumes P is a multiple of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See znlog for algorithmic limitations. Example demonstrates specifying ord vector to initialize curve. Syntax: GEN elllog(GEN E, GEN P, GEN G, GEN o = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: elllseries: deprecated; use lfun(E,s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes value of L-series of E at complex point s (deprecated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses O(N^{1/2}) algorithm where N is conductor. Optional parameter A fixes cutoff to check accuracy; result must be independent of A up to realprecision. Use lfun(E,s) instead. Syntax: GEN elllseries(GEN E, GEN s, GEN A = NULL, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellminimaldisc: minimal discriminant ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the minimal discriminant ideal of elliptic curve E (ellinit output) defined over a number field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: GEN ellminimaldisc(GEN E).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellminimalmodel: determine global minimal integral model or Weierstrass class
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether E (ellinit output over a number field K) admits a global minimal integral model; if so return it and set v=[u,r,s,t] to change-of-variable; otherwise return the (non-principal) Weierstrass class describing obstruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires E defined over Q (D=1 in ellinit) where global minimal model always exists, or over a number field given by bnf structure. Resulting model has integral coefficients and is everywhere minimal; a1,a3 reduced modulo 2; a2 reduced modulo 3. Over Q additionally require a1,a3 in {0,1}, a2 in {0,±1}, and u>0 for uniqueness. Syntax: GEN ellminimalmodel(GEN E, GEN *v = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellminimaltwist: choose discriminant for minimal twist (disc vs conductor)
rubrics_metrics.description: For E/Q, return discriminant D so quadratic twist by D is minimal among all twists: if flag=0 minimal discriminant, if flag=1 minimal conductor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show flag=0 and flag=1 can give different D and resulting minimal discriminant/conductor. Syntaxes: GEN ellminimaltwist0(GEN E, long flag), GEN ellminimaltwist(E) for flag=0, GEN ellminimaltwistcond(E) for flag=1.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellmoddegree: modular degree divided by Manin constant squared
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute modular degree of elliptic curve e defined over Q divided by c^2 where c is Manin constant. Conjecturally c=1 for strong Weil curve; can be proven with ellweilcurve for moderate conductor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate reading ellweilcurve output to deduce Manin constants and modular degrees for isogeny class members. Syntax: GEN ellmoddegree(GEN e).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellmodulareqn: modular equation of level N and types
rubrics_metrics.description: Given prime N<500, return [P,t] where P(x,y) is modular equation of level N and t indicates type: canonical (t=0) or Atkin (t=1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function requires seadata package. Describes functional equation P(f,j)=P(f|WN, j|WN)=0 for chosen modular function f=fN. For canonical type f|WN = N^s / f with s=12/gcd(12,N-1) and f defined via Dedekind eta. Classical modular polynomial Φ_N can be obtained by eliminating f given P; helper classicaleqn(N,X,Y) provided in examples (works for certain N). Syntax: GEN ellmodulareqn(long N, long x = -1, long y = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellmul: scalar multiplication including CM exponents
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute [n]z for point z on E. Exponent n may be integer or a complex quadratic integer if E has complex multiplication by n (otherwise error).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple-minded CM algorithm assumes characteristic 0 and small discriminant quadratic order. Example shows errors when non-CM used. Syntax: GEN ellmul(GEN E, GEN z, GEN n).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellneg: point negation
rubrics_metrics.description: Return opposite of point z on elliptic curve E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: GEN ellneg(GEN E, GEN z).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellnonsingularmultiple: make a multiple have everywhere good reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Given E/Q and rational point P, return [R,n] where n is least positive integer such that R = [n]P has good reduction at every prime (image in minimal model is everywhere non-singular).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show returned R and n. Syntax: GEN ellnonsingularmultiple(GEN E, GEN P).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellorder: order of point with infinite order reported as 0 and optional order hint
rubrics_metrics.description: Return order of point z on E (finite field or number field). Returns 0 if point has infinite order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parameter o is mostly useless and kept for backward compatibility; preferred format [ord, factor(ord)] where ord is curve cardinality. PARI caches curve order in E to avoid recomputing factoring. Obsolete form orderell should not be used. Syntax: GEN ellorder(GEN E, GEN z, GEN o = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellordinate: compute y-coordinates for given x-coordinate
rubrics_metrics.description: Given E and x, return 0,1 or 2-component vector containing y-coordinates of points on E with that x-coordinate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: GEN ellordinate(GEN E, GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellpadicL: compute p-adic L-function values and derivatives with domain sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Return value (or r-th derivative) on a character χ_s of Z_p^* of the p-adic L-function of E/Q twisted by D, given modulo p^n. Characters represented by pair/integers s = (s1,s2) as described; function handles supersingular and ordinary cases differently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When E has good supersingular reduction, L_p values lie in D = H^1_dR(E/Q) ⊗ Q_p and function returns components in basis (ω, F ω) and satisfies (1 - p^{-1}F)^{-2} L_p(E, χ0) = (L(E,1)/Ω)·ω. For ordinary reduction returns projection on α-eigenspace with (1-α^{-1})^{-2} L_p,α(E, χ0) = L(E,1)/Ω. Optional parameter A cutoff (deprecated behavior). Examples show usage for supersingular and ordinary primes; also relates to ms p-adic machinery (mspadicinit, mspadicmoments, mspadicseries). Syntax: GEN ellpadicL(GEN E, GEN p, long n, GEN s = NULL, long r, GEN D = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellpadicbsd: p-adic BSD analog returning analytic rank upper bound and p-adic L-value
rubrics_metrics.description: Given elliptic curve E/Q, its quadratic twist E_D and prime p, compute p-adic analog of ellanalyticrank and ellbsd. Calls ellpadicL and returns [r, Lp] where Lp (or pair if supersingular) is a p-adic number modulo p^N conjecturally equal to R_p * S (R_p = p-adic regulator, S = #Sha for twist), and r is an upper bound for analytic rank of p-adic L-function attached to E_D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains interpretation of r: r-th derivative non-zero modulo p^N, expected relation to Mordell–Weil rank (+1 if split multiplicative at p). If r=0 analytic and Mordell–Weil ranks unconditionally 0. Gives examples for ordinary, non-split multiplicative, split multiplicative and supersingular cases and comparison to ellpadicregulator to infer #Sha. Syntax: GEN ellpadicbsd(GEN E, GEN p, long n, GEN D = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellpadicfrobenius: Frobenius on crystalline module with basis normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: For p>2 and E with good reduction at p, return matrix of Frobenius endomorphism ϕ on crystalline module D_p(E)=Q_p⊗H^1_dR(E/Q) with respect to basis (ω, η=xω). Characteristic polynomial is x^2 - a_p x + p. Matrix computed to absolute p-adic precision p^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows lifting matrix and checking characteristic polynomial and ellap. Syntax: GEN ellpadicfrobenius(GEN E, long p, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellpadicheight: cyclotomic p-adic height vector and reductions for different cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Return cyclotomic p-adic height of rational point P on E/Q as vector [f,g] in D = H^1_dR(E)⊗Q Q_p with respect to basis (ω, η=xω). If Q present, compute bilinear form (h(P+Q)-h(P-Q))/4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If P in kernel of reduction and reductions at finite places non-singular then g = - (log_E P)^2 where log_E is formal group log. For short Weierstrass and P=(x,y), f = log_p(denominator(x)) - 2 log_p(σ(P)) with σ from ellsigma. Normalization note: local and global heights are twice Silverman's. Provides canonical height normalization adjustments: when E has ordinary reduction or non-split multiplicative, canonical height obtained by multiplying by [1,-s2] where s2 = ellpadics2(E,p,n) (compute once); when split multiplicative (Tate curve) extra correction term involving tate parameters. Examples show computing regulator via ellpadicheightmatrix and ellpadics2. Syntax: GEN ellpadicheight0(GEN E, GEN p, long n, GEN P, GEN Q = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellpadicheightmatrix: Gram matrix of cyclotomic p-adic heights
rubrics_metrics.description: Given vector Q of points, return pair [F,G] where F[i,j]=f and G[i,j]=g when ellpadicheight(E,p,n,Q[i],Q[j]) = [f,g]; matrix is given to n p-adic digits with respect to basis (ω,η).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiplying [F,G] by vector [1,-ellpadics2(E,p,n)]^T yields canonical p-adic height Gram matrix. Examples show lifting and arithmetic. Syntax: GEN ellpadicheightmatrix(GEN E, GEN p, long n, GEN Q).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellpadiclog: formal group logarithm for points in kernel of reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: For E defined over K=Q or Q_p and P=[x,y] in kernel of reduction mod p, with t(P) = -x/y the formal group parameter, return L(t) where L is formal logarithm dL = dx/(2y+a1 x + a3) computed to precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate computing for various p and checking required form (P must be in kernel of reduction; sometimes need to replace by 2*P to achieve this). Syntax: GEN ellpadiclog(GEN E, GEN p, long n, GEN P).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellpadicregulator: determinant of Gram matrix and supersingular care
rubrics_metrics.description: Return determinant of Gram matrix of vector of points S with respect to canonical cyclotomic p-adic height on E/Q to n p-adic digits (the p-adic regulator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When E has ordinary reduction, regulator is expected element of Q_p. For supersingular reduction, regulator lies in D = H^1_dR(E)⊗Q_p (2-dim) spanned by ω and η=xω (or ω and F ω); cyclotomic height h_E = f ω + g η defines heights h_η = f and h_ω = -g; R is unique element of D characterized by determinant relation (text cut off in chunk but indicates regulator defined via bilinear/alternating form on D). Syntax: GEN ellpadicregulator(GEN E, GEN p, long n, GEN S).
